questions.q: According to this lesson, why is terraform apply treated differently from a typical application deployment?
options: terraform apply always takes longer than ten minutes to finish running
Application deployments never require any automation at all
An apply can cause destructive, not-easily-reversible changes like deleting a database or replacing a VPC, unlike rolling back a container image
terraform apply cannot be run inside GitHub Actions under any circumstances
questions.explain: Rolling back a bad app deploy is usually quick and safe; a bad apply can destroy or replace infrastructure in ways that aren't simply undone by redeploying something.

questions.q: What does setting `environment: production` on a job in a GitHub Actions workflow actually do?
options: Ties the job to a GitHub Environment's protection rules, pausing it for required-reviewer approval if configured
Changes which cloud region Terraform deploys resources into
Automatically skips the terraform init step
Has no real effect unless the workflow also defines a matrix strategy
questions.explain: environment: production ties the job to a GitHub Environment configured in repository settings, which is where required reviewers are enabled.

questions.q: In the apply workflow shown, what still triggers the job automatically even though a human has to approve the apply itself?
options: Opening a new pull request
A manual click on a 'Run workflow' button every single time
A push to the main branch — on: push: branches: [main]
A scheduled cron job that runs once a week
questions.explain: on: push: branches: [main] still fires the job automatically on every merge; the environment's required reviewers are what pause it before apply actually executes.

questions.q: How does a repository admin configure required reviewers for a GitHub Environment?
options: Required reviewers cannot be configured for GitHub Environments
In Settings → Environments in the GitHub UI, or with a gh api call against the environment, naming reviewers once
By adding a comment to the pull request that says 'please review'
By editing the terraform.tfstate file directly
questions.explain: The reviewer list is set once on the environment itself, either through the Settings UI or a gh api call, and every future run against that environment inherits it.

questions.q: What is Terraform Cloud's equivalent mechanism for gating an apply behind a human?
options: Terraform Cloud has no way to require approval before an apply runs
A workspace set to Manual Apply, which pauses every run after plan until a person clicks Confirm & Apply
Renaming the workspace to include the word 'production'
Setting a longer version constraint in the required_providers block
questions.explain: Terraform Cloud's Manual Apply setting enforces the same plan-then-pause-for-a-human shape as a GitHub Environment's required reviewers, just built into the platform.
